$about: The align-engine manifest (ADR-005). The align/update/self-verify skills read THIS to know what an aligned repo must have - instead of hardcoding it in prose or JS. Paths are the client layout - identical to the standard/ tree in this repo. since names the release that first shipped an entry; unreleased rides the next cut. An aligned repo carries a copy of this file matching the state it last aligned to (a bookmark, never a version it stays at - ADR-025); `scripts/self-verify.mjs` checks the repo against it and reports drift as a number. Method docs are adopted BY REFERENCE, never copied: the `references` section names them at their home in the standards repo (ADR-004/023) - self-verify notes them, checks no files. The repo's copy MAY carry a top-level `profile` field (core|scale, ADR-011) written at align time - self-verify uses it as the default profile. The normative source is SPEC.md; each entry cites the rule it enforces (`rule`). Two fields say what the entry's CONTENT must be, because existence alone is close to no check for the entries whose content is the standard's own: a `copy` entry carries `sha256` - a hash string for a file, one hash per member for a directory - generated by tools/manifest-hashes.mjs and verified by tools/tree-check.mjs, never hand-written, and self-verify hashes the local file against it (CRLF normalized to LF; the manifest itself carries none, since a file cannot hold its own hash; a member missing from a directory entry is reported the same way a changed one is, so a required item quietly removed is a content failure, not a silent pass); a `merge` entry, which is adapted on purpose and so cannot be hashed, MAY declare `requiredKeys` - dotted key paths that must be present in the merged result (JSON objects and YAML block mappings; presence only, never a value). A deliberate, recorded deviation goes in `exceptions`: { "kind": "file"|"section"|"content"|"key", "match": "<path>" for a file or its content, "<file>#<heading>" for a section, "<file>#<key.path>" for a key, "reason": "..." } - self-verify.mjs reports it as excepted rather than drift (R17), keeps it in the adoption denominator so excepting can never raise the percentage, and prints the count in the summary. The hatch is bounded: there is no `guard` kind (a guard is a live check - waiving its verdict removes it instead of recording a deviation from it), a guard's own script file cannot be excepted by `kind: "file"` (a missing guard script is skipped, so that would disable a blocking check at drift 0 - use `kind: "content"`, which keeps the guard running), and an exception with no `reason` is not a recorded one.

adaptRules.copy: ship verbatim; the repo gets a byte-for-byte copy (guards, templates that carry no repo-specific content)
adaptRules.merge: combine the standard's content with what the repo already has, keeping both (ignore files, CI that already has jobs)
adaptRules.fill-from-repo: scaffold the shell from the standard, then author the body from THIS repo's reality - never blind-copy the example prose (ARCHITECTURE, PRODUCT, specs)
adaptRules.reference: do not copy; link to the living standard - always latest (ADR-004/025 - the standard's own decisions reach clients by reference)

the normative core this manifest projects - readable in place

the work ledger; items leave only when their DoD is met
the only home of history (ADR-018); a PR describes its change under `## Unreleased` and never touches the version - R18/R25's one path, at every profile
the verify step - checks the repo against this manifest
spec layout guard
a fact restated in prose still agrees with its source - declared homes and claims (R4)

the secret-scan workflow template
weekly notification that a newer standard exists - opens one issue per release, never edits the recorded state (ADR-025)
agent settings baseline - permission lists, and which guards run
forces LF on the shipped bash guards and Node scripts - a repo whose own setting is eol=crlf makes every hook exit 127 with empty stdout, which for a deny-guard is silence, not a refusal
the pre-execution guards themselves: remote-DB writes, force-push, CI secrets
drives every guard with real commands - they only emit output on a denial, so a broken guard is otherwise silent
the altitude apex R1 names - optional but expected
code<->spec coupling guard (+ --audit) - the tool ships at core, the blocking CI gate is scale (R11)
the CI workflow that wires self-verify + both guards - how R16's gate actually runs
the persona roster the R10 gate checks specs against - without it the gate has nothing to hold
the repo's front door - authored from this repo's reality
contribution mechanics pointer - defers to AGENTS.md
vulnerability-reporting contact and posture (placeholders filled at adoption)
exact runtime version for the dependency-free guards and CI setup
PR template - what/why, ADR impact, test plan, checklist
the docs hub table
how it is built - the altitude names it (filled from this repo)
what it is and where it is going (filled from this repo)
canonical conventions block - merged into AGENTS.md at adoption
event-taxonomy tracking plan template
per-persona journey maps coupled to capabilities
anonymized research studies feeding personas, ideas and specs
operational runbooks + postmortems - agent-followable at 3 a.m.

proves the one-place invariant the pool and the cycles depend on

guards.purpose: spec files are where and shaped as the standard requires
declared facts still agree with their source (skips itself where none are declared)
the schema and its typed twin have not drifted (skips itself where there is no database)
domain code changed without touching its spec fails CI
an intent is in the backlog pool or in exactly one cycle (skips itself where there are no cycles)
the ADR/BDR index and the directory on disk agree - duplicate id, orphaned index row, or unindexed record all fail

decisions.prompt: Where are the module/domain seams? (slice by capability, not layer)
Test tiers and where each runs?
The floor below which nothing ships?

specs.tierDecision: Could an agent rebuild and verify this capability from the spec alone, without reading the code? If yes -> buildable; behavioral is an escape hatch that must be justified in-spec and stays rare.
